items.followUp: Write 72000 m and 0.0045 s in standard form.
Define translatory motion and give one example.

rubric.why: The definition must identify the path followed by the moving body.
rubric.description: Defines circular motion as motion along a circular path.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the body moves along a circular path.

rubric.why: A correct example demonstrates understanding of the motion.
rubric.description: Gives one suitable example of circular motion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any valid example, such as a rotating wheel or a clock hand.

modelAnswer: Circular motion is the motion of a body along a circular path.
Example: The hands of a clock move in circular motion.

items.followUp: Define velocity and write its SI unit.

rubric.why: Speed describes how much distance is covered in a given time.
rubric.description: Defines speed as distance travelled per unit time.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for relating distance travelled to time taken.

rubric.why: The SI unit expresses distance in metres and time in seconds.
rubric.description: States the SI unit of speed.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for m/s or an equivalent notation.

modelAnswer: Speed is the distance travelled by a body per unit time.
The SI unit of speed is metre per second (m/s).

items.followUp: Define acceleration and write its SI unit.

rubric.why: Acceleration measures how velocity changes with time.
rubric.description: Defines acceleration as the rate of change of velocity with time.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for relating change in velocity to time.

rubric.why: The SI unit follows from velocity change per unit time.
rubric.description: States the SI unit of acceleration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for m/s² or an equivalent notation.

modelAnswer: Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity with time.
The SI unit of acceleration is metre per second squared (m/s²).

items.followUp: What is the resolution of a force into rectangular components?

rubric.why: Resolution means replacing a force by component forces.
rubric.description: States that resolution is the process of splitting a force into components.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing a force as split or resolved into components.

rubric.why: The components must together represent the original force.
rubric.description: States that the components together have the same effect as the original force.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for noting that the combined effect of the components equals that of the original force.

modelAnswer: The resolution of forces is the process of splitting a force into two or more component forces.
These components together have the same effect as the original force.

items.followUp: State the principle of moments for a body in equilibrium.

rubric.why: The principle compares the moments acting in opposite directions.
rubric.description: States that clockwise moments equal anticlockwise moments.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the equality of clockwise and anticlockwise moments.

rubric.why: The principle applies to a body in equilibrium and moments are taken about a point.
rubric.description: Specifies the equilibrium condition or the point about which moments are considered.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning equilibrium or moments about the same point.

modelAnswer: For a body in equilibrium, the sum of the clockwise moments about a point is equal to the sum of the anticlockwise moments about the same point.

items.followUp: Define power and state its SI unit.

rubric.why: Work is calculated from force and displacement in the force's direction.
rubric.description: Defines work as the product of force and displacement in the direction of the force.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating the force–displacement relationship.

rubric.why: The SI unit of work is the joule, equivalent to a newton metre.
rubric.description: States the SI unit of work.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for joule (J) or an equivalent unit.

modelAnswer: Work is done when a force causes displacement in its direction.
Work is equal to the product of force and displacement in the direction of the force.
The SI unit of work is the joule (J).

items.followUp: Define kinetic energy and give its formula.

rubric.why: Kinetic energy is associated with the motion of a body.
rubric.description: Defines kinetic energy as energy due to motion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking kinetic energy with a body's motion.

rubric.why: Potential energy is associated with position or configuration.
rubric.description: Defines potential energy as energy due to position or configuration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking potential energy with position or configuration.

modelAnswer: Kinetic energy is the energy possessed by a body due to its motion.
Potential energy is the energy possessed by a body due to its position or configuration.
